name: Comfrey extract
description: Comfrey extract (CAS 84696-05-9 ), derived from Symphytum officinale, is a botanical active used across personal care, pharmaceutical, and nutraceutical formulations. It delivers moisturizing, skin-conditioning, and antioxidant activity. This makes it a sought-after ingredient for formulators working with plant-derived actives. In topical cosmetic formulations such as creams, balms, and serums, it functions as a humectant and skin-conditioning agent. The extract supports moisture retention and surface repair in various skincare applications. Pharmaceutical and healthcare product developers incorporate it into topical preparations such as ointments and gels. These products often target joint and muscle discomfort through specialized delivery systems. In hair care, it is used in conditioners and scalp treatments where its botanical actives contribute to softening performance. Nutraceutical and food supplement manufacturers also source it for inclusion in botanical blends. In these applications, antioxidant support is the primary formulation objective for the final consumer product. The material is supplied as a liquid extract, dry powder, or glycerin-based solution depending on solvent compatibility. Standard grades include cosmetic-grade and food-grade specifications for diverse needs. Concentration levels are typically expressed as dry extract ratios or standardized active content. Buyers should confirm pyrrolizidine alkaloid content compliance with applicable regional regulatory limits. Selecting the correct grade for topical or ingestible use ensures safety and efficacy.
